knowledgeAnswers.rationale: An out-of-date reagent can give an unreliable result. The tester replaces it, retests and records the replacement. Recording the colour as valid is not acceptable.
The record must show that no valid test was done in that period, with the reason. Back-filling or estimating creates a false record.
Reagents are chemicals. They are stored away from acids and oxidisers, as the SDS directs, and never in food or drink containers.
The taking the sample section says to use the sampling location, depth and method in the operator plan.

practicalCriteria: Sample record: on a supplied sampling scenario, the learner records the time, location, depth, method, unit and tester for each result. The assessor checks that each field is complete.
Correction: the learner corrects one supplied error by a single line, initials, date and reason, with the original still legible. The assessor checks that no entry was overwritten or deleted.

Invalid test: for a supplied expired reagent, the learner records the test as invalid, replaces the reagent and records the retest. The assessor checks that the expired result is not recorded as valid.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 2 of 3 correct (a reading result only, not verified practical competence). Practical sign-off is separate and is given by assessor review of the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Completed sample record and correction log, saved and dated
Assessor sign-off on the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: The learner is asked to back-fill a missed test
A reagent is past expiry and the learner is asked to record the result as valid
Reagents are being stored beside acid or oxidiser products
